function.mechanism: Displaces oxygen in package headspace and acts as a chemically inert gas, reducing oxidation and helping preserve food quality.

adi.basis: EFSA FAF (2024) concluded no safety concern for E938 and did not establish a numerical ADI.

efsa.key_finding: Re-evaluation concluded that use of argon (E938) as a food additive does not raise a safety concern; low toxicological concern based on physicochemical inertness.

fda.cfr_citation: No specific Title 21 food-additive/GRAS section for argon identified in queried eCFR food sections; argon hits were in medical device sections (e.g., 21 CFR 868.1075).

adi.basis: Current queried WHO JECFA argon entry/API outputs did not provide a numerical ADI for argon.

concerns.summary: Main uncertainty is data completeness (limited submitted use-level and impurity information), rather than a demonstrated toxicological hazard signal in food-use context.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA FAF (2024) concluded E938 use does not raise a safety concern.
Argon is chemically inert and treated as low toxicological concern in the EFSA re-evaluation.
No IARC monograph classification identified for argon.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI is available for E938 in the reviewed sources; practical exceedance concern appears low given packaging-gas/propellant use pattern and expected low dietary intake.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence is favorable (EFSA 2024 no-safety-concern conclusion), with inert chemistry and no carcinogenic classification signal identified; remaining uncertainty is mainly sparse modern oral-toxicity and impurity-use data rather than positive hazard findings.
key_factors: EFSA 2024 re-evaluation found no safety concern for E938
Limited submitted impurity/use-level data in re-evaluation
